Thanks for the context, Priyom. Quick summary from legal: we can accommodate the 30-day uplift and a one-time credit but prefer an Order Form supplement rather than an amendment to the MSA for speed. Key points to include in the redline: 

1) Scope and duration: explicitly state the uplift window start/end dates and that uplift reverts to baseline committed throughput after the window.
2) Credit mechanics: a one-time, non-recurring credit equal to measured overage (as defined by token/throughput metering) during the uplift window; credit to be applied to the immediately subsequent invoice. No retroactive discounts beyond the single window.
3) Liability / SLA carve-out: call out that burst capacity during the onboarding window is best-effort and does not change SLA entitlements; include an upper safety throttle clause.
4) Termination: allow either party to terminate the supplement with 5 business days' notice if usage materially exceeds reasonable expectations.

I've attached legal_redlines_summary.pdf with suggested language (trackable changes in the Word doc look good). Recommend we avoid cash refunds — credit only — and avoid perpetual pricing concessions. Also: operations will need a ticket to configure the temporary throughput profile in our provisioning system.

If you want, I can paste short-form legal language into the order form now and we can route via DocuSign. Otherwise confirm and I'll create the final supplement.

-Karthik
